title: Store ticket states so the next release reads them right

blocks.text: The support desk keeps each ticket's state in a text column of the tickets table. The next release adds two states, `TRIAGED` and `WAITING`, and the table already holds a few hundred thousand rows written by the current one (`PreviousState` in the starter). Nobody wants to migrate them.
Finish `write` and `read` in `src/main/java/practice/TicketStore.java`. `write` turns a state of either release into the column's text; `read` turns that text back into a `State` of the new release.

When you're done, every row the previous release wrote loads as the state it was saved as, and every state of the new release, `WAITING` included, survives a save and a load. About two lines in total.

cases.says: a state saved by this release loads back as the same state
saving a ticket again replaces the state the store loads
a row the previous release wrote loads as the same state in this release, which declares new constants before it
a state whose toString() is display text still loads back as itself

origin.section: An Ordinal Is a Position, and Inserting a Constant Moves It

concepts: A stored ordinal points at another constant once a constant is inserted, removed or reordered, so what leaves the JVM is the name (not a display toString) or a code of your own.
